 On Thursday, Gloria’s Foundation and fashion marketplace Weldun hosted a group of 25 women from Steinem’s circle for an intimate dinner celebrating her life and legacy at her home on the Upper East Side.
Dinner attendees included Former Secretary of State Hillary Rodham Clinton, Naomi Watts , Shonda Rhimes, Melissa McCarthy, Mariska Hargitay, Paloma Elsesser, Bethann Hardison, Racquel Chevremont, Paola Kudacki, Carly Berlin, Padma Lakshmi, Karis Jagger and more.
The evening began with cocktails and mingling in Steinem’s bedroom surrounded by the artwork, keepsakes and distinct design that shaped her home life. For the evening, the foundation staged black-and-white portraits of Steinem by Paola Kudacki throughout her home. These photos were taken in May in collaboration with the new brand Weldun, a marketplace for women with evolving physical needs, be it from injuries, disabilities, aging, or anything else. These photographs became Steinem’s final portraits before her passing in September.

 “I had met Gloria at one of her Talking Circles about women’s health about six months prior,” said Weldun founder Carly Berlin. “So much of what we do is talking about women having the freedom and autonomy over their own bodies, regardless of the bodies they’re in. I was thinking about who would be my absolute dream person to feature for first Weldun voices series, which is a quarterly series we do. And Gloria just kept popping into my mind. She was 92 at the time. She embodied so many seasons of a woman’s life in the women that we were speaking to.” 
Hardison shared stories of her travels around the world, groundbreaking modeling career, and the impact Steinem’s activism had on her life. Although she had never been to her home before, Hardison knew Steinem personally and could tell simply by being in her space, that “Gloria was THAT girl.”
“Meeting her and photographing her was so special, because she’s an icon, and it’s crazy that, as women, we’re still fighting for our rights, and as humans, we still fighting for our rights. She dedicated her whole life to fight for us and continued to fight until the last day,” said Kudacki. “It was so inspiring to meet somebody, so passionate about mission in life.”
 Lux Pascal and Naomi Watts 
 Jeanette D. Moses/WWD 
 “To have one of my daughters with me and to realize who’s in this room and what it means to be a feminist and support women and love women, which is all being a feminist means, it just was amazing to be here tonight,” said McCarthy. “I kept getting overwhelmed with different amazing people.”
“Gloria was an incredible mentor to me,” Rhimes said. “I think she was an incredible mentor to everybody. And coming here tonight was such a beautiful way to honor her. Also to get an opportunity to kind of stand in her shoes. I’m really glad I had the opportunity.”
